alt.en: Two lines of printed music numbered 204 and marked "Slow.", a voice line over a piano part with two flats in 3/4 time, with the words "So Farewell to you ye fine Spanish Ladies So farewell to you ye Ladies of Spain, For we've receiv'd orders to sail for Old England And perhaps we may never come back here again."
alt.es: Dos sistemas de música impresa con el número 204 y la indicación "Slow.", una línea de voz sobre una parte de piano con dos bemoles en compás de 3/4, con la letra "So Farewell to you ye fine Spanish Ladies So farewell to you ye Ladies of Spain, For we've receiv'd orders to sail for Old England And perhaps we may never come back here again."

caption.en: No. 204 in William Chappell's Collection of National English Airs (London, 1840), marked "Slow": the tune in print, in a minor key with the raised seventh that Sharp's 1909 version leaves out.
caption.es: El n.º 204 de la Collection of National English Airs de William Chappell (Londres, 1840), marcado "Slow" (lento): la melodía impresa, en tonalidad menor y con la séptima elevada que la versión de Sharp de 1909 no tiene.

source: W. Chappell, ed., A Collection of National English Airs (London: Chappell; Simpkin, Marshall & Co., 1840), p. 98, No. 204, "So Farewell to you ye fine Spanish Ladies" (detail of the page)
library: Music Library, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: UNC b7453895; Internet Archive collectionofnati00crot, scan image n123
licenceEvidence: Published London 1840. Editor William Chappell died 1888; the harmony marked "M." is G. A. Macfarren's (died 1887); co-editors William Crotch died 1847 and J. A. Wade died 1845. Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).
credit: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill Music Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A printed page of music headed "CXXIV. Spanish Ladies. Sea Chanty.", marked Moderato, page 62: a voice line in 3/4 time over a two-stave piano part, with the first verse under the notes, from "Farewell and adieu to you Spanish ladies" to "But we hope in a short time to see you again."
alt.es: Página de música impresa con el encabezado "CXXIV. Spanish Ladies. Sea Chanty.", marcada Moderato, página 62: una línea de voz en compás de 3/4 sobre una parte de piano en dos pentagramas, con la primera estrofa bajo las notas, desde "Farewell and adieu to you Spanish ladies" hasta "But we hope in a short time to see you again."

caption.en: Spanish Ladies as No. 124 in Cecil J. Sharp's Folk Songs from Somerset, Fifth Series (London, 1909), from the singing of Captain Lewis of Minehead: the voice part our soprano sings note for note.
caption.es: Spanish Ladies como n.º 124 de Folk Songs from Somerset, Fifth Series, de Cecil J. Sharp (Londres, 1909), tal como la cantaba el capitán Lewis, de Minehead: la parte vocal que nuestra soprano canta nota por nota.

source: Cecil J. Sharp, Folk Songs from Somerset, Fifth Series (London: Simpkin & Co.; Schott & Co.; Taunton: Barnicott and Pearce, 1909), No. CXXIV, "Spanish Ladies. Sea Chanty", p. 62
library: Sibley Music Library, Eastman School of Music, University of Rochester (via IMSLP and the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Published London 1909. Editor and arranger Cecil J. Sharp died 1924; the words on this page (verse 1) are traditional and in print before 1859. Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).
credit: Sibley Music Library, Eastman School of Music, via IMSLP and the Internet Archive

alt.en: An old engraved sea chart crossed by compass lines, with Brittany on the left and Cornwall and Devon on the right, the Scilly isles at the top right, and a plain title box at the lower left naming the third part of the Channel between England and France, published in Amsterdam by Joannes van Keulen.
alt.es: Antigua carta náutica grabada, cruzada por líneas de rumbo, con Bretaña a la izquierda y Cornualles y Devon a la derecha, las islas Scilly arriba a la derecha y, abajo a la izquierda, un recuadro sencillo con el título de la tercera parte del canal entre Inglaterra y Francia, publicada en Ámsterdam por Joannes van Keulen.

caption.en: A Dutch sea chart of the western Channel from the Van Keulen firm of Amsterdam, with Ushant ("Isle Douessant") and the Scilly isles, the two sides of the Channel's mouth in the chorus, and the Dodman ("Dootmans hooft") and Rame Head, the first land of the older verses.
caption.es: Carta náutica holandesa de la parte occidental del canal de la Mancha, de la casa Van Keulen de Ámsterdam, con Ushant ("Isle Douessant") y las islas Scilly, los dos lados de la boca del canal en el estribillo, y el Dodman ("Dootmans hooft") y Rame Head, la primera tierra de las estrofas antiguas.

source: Paskaart van Het Kanaal tussen Engeland en Frankrijk, deel 3 (title on the sheet: "Nieuwe Zeekaart van t derde Gedeelte van t Canaal tusschen Engeland en Vrankryk"; "t Amsterdam By Ioannes van Keulen ... Opgestelt door Gerard van Keulen")
licenceEvidence: Rijksmuseum record https://data.rijksmuseum.nl/200396063?_profile=dc gives rights https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/ (Public Domain Mark), date "1688 - 1803". Compiler Gerard van Keulen died 1726; printed by 1803 at the latest (see rights.md).

alt.en: A sepia photograph looking down from high chalk cliffs: a dark, grassy slope on the left, two tall chalk pinnacles in the middle, and a beach and a calm, hazy sea far below.
alt.es: Fotografía en sepia tomada desde lo alto de unos acantilados de creta: una ladera oscura cubierta de hierba a la izquierda, dos agujas de creta altas en el centro y, muy abajo, una playa y un mar tranquilo y brumoso.

caption.en: Beachy Head, near Eastbourne, photographed in April 1900: in the older verses, the homeward ship sails "by Beachy" on its way up the Channel to the Downs.
caption.es: Beachy Head, cerca de Eastbourne, fotografiado en abril de 1900: en las estrofas antiguas, el barco que vuelve a casa pasa "by Beachy" (junto a Beachy) en su camino por el canal hasta los Downs.

source: Gezicht op Beachy Head nabij Eastbourne, East Sussex (photograph on paper, anonymous, dated 14 April 1900)
licenceEvidence: Rijksmuseum record https://data.rijksmuseum.nl/200324891?_profile=dc gives rights https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/ (Public Domain Mark), creator anonymous, date "1900-04-14". Anonymous photograph of 1900: PD by age (see rights.md).
